comments.body: The correction says no number is safe to act on, but the active “Narrowed form” paragraph immediately above still defines the rule with “a frozen baseline — of the 263 uncited claims.” That leaves the design’s normative description inconsistent; update that paragraph to the per-document `claims_in`/`UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS` baseline instead of only appending a correction below.

reviews.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer[bot]
reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended The R10-D6 checker mismatch and registry-test gap remain unresolved, alongside stale baseline instructions in the planning documents. *Get a fresh assessment by requesting another Copilot review.*
Pull request overview This PR formalizes leg B’s claim predicate and registers `R10-D5` and `R10-D6` in the rule registry. **Changes:** - Adds claim-scope definitions and registry tests. - Registers two rule rows and moves a runtime citation. - Updates planning documents with revised baselines and backfill details.
File summaries | File | Summary and review notes | |---|---| | `tests/test_rule_registry.py` | Adds predicate and registry coverage. **Moderate (1 vote):** the pack-noun test can pass with a hard-coded roster; it should stub `pack_nouns()` and assert a sentinel is recognized. | | `docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/prd.md` | Updates baseline requirements. **Nit (1 vote):** active acceptance text still asserts the unreproducible 263 baseline. | | `docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/implement.md` | Records implementation progress. **Nit (1 vote):** the checklist still instructs verification against the obsolete 263→264 baseline. | | `docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/design.md` | Documents predicate semantics and risks. **Nits (2 votes, 1 vote):** active text retains the 263 baseline, and `claims_in` is conflated with the derived `UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS` projection. | | `bin/sd_setup_github.py` | Moves the rule citation out of runtime text. | | `bin/sd_rules.py` | Registers the two rule rows. **Moderate (2 votes):** `sd_lib.repo_root` does not enforce the R10-D6 invariant because it accepts an optional start path. |
Review details ### Suppressed comments (4) **docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/design.md:50** * These lines identify the wrong contract: `claims_in` returns a list of every matching `(line, run, rule ids)` tuple, while `UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS` is produced by `uncited_skill_claims()` after filtering to empty `ids` and counting per document. Calling the dictionary what `claims_in` returns can send the next baseline update to the wrong value; please make this wording, and the matching comment in `tests/test_rule_registry.py`, describe it as a projection instead. ``` `source:tests/test_rule_registry.py::claims_in` — and the only figure recorded anywhere is `UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS`, which is what that function returns. ``` **docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/implement.md:32** * Appending this correction does not update the live checklist above it: that text still tells implementers the baseline is 263 and to verify a 263→264 mutation. Those are now unreproducible verification steps and can make future work validate the wrong predicate; replace the old checklist wording with the per-document `claims_in` baseline and its control. ``` > **Correction, 2026-09-12 (sd:622).** 263 could not be reproduced, and > the three readings offered in its place could not be reproduced either: > an independent reconstruction of the same three shapes gave different > figures again, because each reconstruction had to invent the counting > rule the original never recorded. The shape of the requirement is ``` **docs/work/2026-09-12-every-rule-is-a-row-and-a-checker/prd.md:141** * The correction supersedes the 263 baseline, but the active acceptance text immediately above still says the uncited shape is “263 of the 264 claims in skills/ today.” That leaves the PRD asserting an unreproducible current count even though this new block says no such number is safe to act on; update the remaining acceptance references to describe `claims_in`/`UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS` instead. ``` - [x] ~~The leg b baseline is 263~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12 by sd:622: 263 cannot be reproduced and neither can its proposed replacements.** The baseline is what `claims_in` returns, held per document in `UNCITED_SKILL_CLAIMS`, and a test asserts it may fall and may not rise. The control asserting that a *correctly cited* claim does not redden it ``` **tests/test_rule_registry.py:920** * This still does not test the invariant it describes: a hard-coded pattern containing all current `pack_nouns()` values (or extra values) satisfies the subset/`missed` assertions, so `names_a_pack_noun` can carry its own roster while the test stays green. Stub `pack_nouns()` to return a sentinel while constructing the matcher and assert that the sentinel is recognized, so a listed roster is actually caught. ``` subject = names_a_pack_noun() missed = sorted(name for name in nouns if not subject.search(f"the {name} tool")) self.assertEqual(missed, [], f""" The claim subject does not match every name enumerated from the tree. ``` - **Files reviewed:** 4/6 changed files - **Comments generated:** 1 - **Review effort level:** Lite
